codeReview.summary: Clean, well-structured implementation that adds dispatcher-specific command building to the engine type system. The DispatcherCommandOptions interface is cleanly separated from EngineCommandOptions. Both engine providers implement buildDispatcherCommand() correctly with appropriate optimization flags. Claude uses -p for direct prompt passing (no stdin), --tools '' to disable tools, --system-prompt for caching, --no-session-persistence, and --effort low. OpenCode uses the existing stdin pattern with --model and --format json. The implementation is additive — worker buildCommand() is completely untouched. Tests are comprehensive (24 tests) covering both engines, defaults, custom models, negative cases for flag isolation, and registry integration. The downstream SubprocessTransport in both dispatcher and evaluator correctly consume buildDispatcherCommand() via the DispatcherCommandOptions interface.

issues.description: OpenCode buildDispatcherCommand() accepts a systemPrompt parameter via DispatcherCommandOptions but silently ignores it — the system prompt is not passed as any CLI flag or included in args. This works because the downstream SubprocessTransport manually concatenates systemPrompt into stdin content for OpenCode, but the interface suggests the engine handles it. A code comment noting this design decision (e.g., 'systemPrompt is not used here — caller prepends it to stdin') would improve clarity for future maintainers.
The EngineCommandOptions import (line 5) is unused — it's imported as a type but never referenced in the test file. Minor lint issue only.

OpenCode dispatcher does not attempt any tool restriction (no --agent flag or prompt prefix to disable tools). The feature description noted 'investigate --agent flag or accept that OpenCode may not support tool disabling easily. At minimum, pass --model.' The worker accepted the minimum approach. This is reasonable given OpenCode CLI limitations, but the lack of tool disabling means OpenCode dispatchers may be slower than Claude dispatchers due to unnecessary tool availability.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The AGENTS.md in the mission dir documents Claude CLI flags well but does not mention that OpenCode's buildDispatcherCommand ignores the systemPrompt parameter by design (relying on the caller to prepend it to stdin). This asymmetry between engine providers is an architectural decision worth documenting.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/engines/providers/opencode/index.ts:84-100 — buildDispatcherCommand does not reference options.systemPrompt. Compare to src/engines/providers/claude/index.ts:94 which uses --system-prompt flag. The SubprocessTransport at src/dispatcher/subprocess-transport.ts:115-119 compensates by prepending systemPrompt to stdin for OpenCode.

summary: PASS. The engine-dispatcher-command-building feature is correctly implemented. The DispatcherCommandOptions interface and buildDispatcherCommand() method are cleanly added to the Engine type system without affecting existing worker command building. Both Claude and OpenCode providers produce correct commands with appropriate optimization flags. The 24 new tests provide thorough coverage including flag verification, default models, custom model overrides, worker isolation checks, and registry integration. The only notable design observation is that OpenCode silently ignores the systemPrompt parameter (handled by the caller instead), which works correctly but could benefit from a clarifying comment. No blocking issues found.
